title: Retries with a shared deadline
summary: Retry transient failures with capped backoff while passing each attempt the remaining time from one budget.
code: def retry(operation, *, attempts, budget, clock, sleep):
raise ValueError("positive attempt and time budgets required")
if attempt == attempts or delay >= deadline - clock():
triggers: retry transient failures within a total latency budget
cap exponential backoff and avoid starting retries after a deadline
prompts: Give a dependency several chances within one caller deadline and pass each attempt its own remaining timeout.
Stop retrying when the next backoff would spend all of the remaining time, even if attempts remain.
invariant: All attempts share one monotonic deadline. A retry starts only if time and attempts remain, and only transient failures can trigger it.
mantra: One deadline; spend it across every attempt and wait.
pitfalls: Starting a fresh timeout for every attempt can exceed the caller’s total budget. The operation must enforce the timeout it receives.
A timeout does not tell you whether a write took effect. Retry only safe operations or use an idempotency key.
This example uses deterministic delays. Add jitter when many clients can retry at the same time.

anchors.name: Shared deadline
anchors.trick: Subtract the current monotonic time before each attempt and after each failure.

anchors.name: Retry amplification
anchors.trick: Limit retries at one layer so nested retries do not multiply work.

mutations.replacement: if attempt == attempts or delay > deadline - clock():
mutations.explanation: Sleeping exactly until the deadline leaves no time for another attempt and loses the original error.

test: now[0] += 0.1  # The attempt itself spends part of the budget.
assert retry(flaky, attempts=3, budget=1, clock=lambda: now[0], sleep=sleep) == "ok"
retry(invalid, attempts=3, budget=1, clock=lambda: now[0], sleep=sleep)
